text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Campaigning for local council elections starts.
- Interior Minister Driss Basri hands national commission in charge of elections a list of alleged irregularities made since registration of voters started.
- Morocco calls on voters to collect electoral cards.
- Highway linking Casablanca to nearby city of Settat will cost 1.84 billion dirhams ($197 million).
- Spain gives Morocco 19 million dirhams ($2 million) for water projects in northern city of Chefachaouen.
- Fisheries, Merchant Navy Minister Mustapha Sahel tells seminar on fisheries industries that Morocco is looking for real partnership through investments and creation of joint ventures.
- Spanish forum on ways to tackle illegal immigration flow on its southern frontiers reveals there is a bigger influx via the Pyrenees mountains in the north.
- General Confederation of Moroccan Businesses (CGEM) to elect new president on July 4.
- The Stock Exchange's downward corrections make shares more attractive for potential buyers.
- Morocco rules out renewal of EU fish accord despite attempt by European Fisheries Commissioner Emma Bonino to raise issue.
